## TL;DR

This session resumed review repair for the restart notice defect. The implementation in the worktree detects systemd and launchd supervisors independently of the server's process title, invokes the detected supervisor's restart operation, and waits for a healthy replacement. It reports restart command failures to the UI. I reviewed those paths and their tests, confirmed the progress/error UI and fixtures, and recorded that live hand-run restart QA was not performed. A scoped check is still required; this draft must not be treated as verified until that check passes.

## Work and rationale

The latest review identified two related supervisor-routing failures. Detection could recognize a RepoOS unit through its cgroup or parent process but lose the unit identity before restart classification. External supervisors were also handled by stopping the old process and hoping that the manager recreated it. Both behaviors could leave the server unavailable or report “hand-run” despite a supervisor owning the process.

The worktree now carries the unit identity and restart metadata from detection through execution. Linux detection records the unit and whether it belongs to the user manager; the parent fallback recognizes a `systemd --user` parent and builds the corresponding user-unit command. Darwin detection retains the launchd label and its domain-qualified restart command. The classifier directs identified managed and external units through a supervisor route, except where the registered RepoOS service already provides the correct managed-service path. Ambiguous detection remains fail-closed.

The restart operation calls `systemctl restart` or `launchctl kickstart -k` using executable/argument arrays. It does not shell out through a constructed command string and it does not signal the supervised PID first. It waits for the expected listener to return healthy with a new PID. If command execution fails, the result includes a direct error and manual command; if the command succeeds but the server does not return, the result explains that distinction. The release notice has progress state, clears progress if the request fails, and displays the returned failure text. It also has preview states for progress and service error so the declared shots can be captured.

The detection and restart tests cover systemd user units, a renamed process whose parent is systemd when cgroup inspection fails, launchd, hand-run servers, supervisor command invocation, failure surfacing, and timeout behavior. The UI fixture test checks that the progress and error states are accepted as dialog captures. Existing QA documentation records the restart verification limits; this session added a further explicit note that a real hand-run restart was not performed.

## Approaches tried

I inspected the task's current worktree changes, the latest review findings supplied with the task, the restart classifier and executor, detector tests, the release notice, fixture registration, and the existing QA record. I retained the direct-supervisor approach already present in the branch rather than restoring PID termination and relying on KeepAlive behavior. A service manager owns restart policy, so requesting the restart from that manager is the reliable way to exercise it.

I also checked whether the UI states or QA note were absent. The UI already showed progress and rendered a role-alert error with the supplied restart command. Both shot states are in the shared fixture catalog and have a test. The QA record already said that no real restart had been performed; I added a current-session entry to make that evidence explicit rather than implying a live check had occurred.

## Challenges and blockers

The worktree initially retained merge metadata after its conflicts had been resolved. That caused the previous partial checkpoint attempt to fail with “cannot do a partial commit during a merge.” I cleared only the stale merge metadata with `git merge --quit`, preserving the index and working tree; RepoOS then created its normal WIP checkpoint. Sibling task bookkeeping was left for RepoOS's foreign-file handoff healing rather than manually rewritten here.

`REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed in this session. The local check passed staleness, format, lint, build freshness, CSS checks, contrast audit, branch-artifact and task-asset guards, and headless UI smoke. Remote validation passed all 579 changed test files (8,219 passed, one skipped), the separate boot-timing suite (2 passed), rendered contrast, and headless UI smoke. A real hand-run or supervised server was not available to operate, so the QA record makes no claim of live restart success. Automated tests are not a substitute for that operator observation.

## Key learnings

Supervisor detection must return enough information to execute the correct operation later: platform, unit identity, and scope/domain. A process name is not authoritative when wrappers rename it. Likewise, stopping a PID is not equivalent to restarting its owner; supervised processes should be restarted by the manager and then verified through the service's health endpoint.

UI fixtures need registration in the common shot fixture catalog as well as component behavior, otherwise a visually correct state still cannot be captured during review. Finally, QA notes should distinguish automated regression coverage from an observed live restart. Here, live restart evidence remains absent and is explicitly identified as such.
